transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Time: 15:27 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Kim, Priya Shah, Maya Ortiz (Redwood); Laura Meier, Tomás Alvarez, Marta Novak, Erik Sorensen (NordicBank)

Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): discussion focused on data residency and region pinning for NordicBank regulated workloads; SOC2/ISO evidence, sub-processors, encryption (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and required configuration for EU-only processing were covered. Next steps and action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Looks like we have Laura, Tomás, Marta, Erik from NordicBank; and Priya, Maya and myself from Redwood. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, region pinning, sub-processor list, and any legal questions.
[00:23] Laura Meier: Hi all, yep that's correct. We're particularly focused on ensuring PII and customer data for EU customers stays in the EU. We also need to understand cross-border processing for metadata and logs.
[00:45] Priya Shah: Perfect, we'll start with the region pinning capabilities. Redwood supports explicit region pinning at the route level, you can pin requests to EU regions only, so no processing in US data centers. There are two modes: hosted EU-only and private (VPC) where control is with you.
[01:10] Tomás Alvarez: When you say "hosted EU-only" does that mean our data never egresses to the US, including logs, telemetry, and backups?
[01:25] Priya Shah: For hosted EU-only, we ensure model inference and request processing happen in EU regions. Logs and audit trails can also be restricted to EU, we have retention zones. There are caveats around global control plane metadata for multi-tenant hosted -- some control plane telemetry may be routed to our control plane which is multi-region, but customer data and payloads remain in pinned regions.
[01:52] Martha? Speaker mismatch
[01:55] Marta Novak: Sorry, Marta here. That "control plane" distinction is important for legal. We need to see a clear split: no customer content leaves the EU in any circumstance without signed agreement.
[02:10] Jesse Kim: That's fair. We have contract language for strict region commitments and also offer Redwood Private where you get a private control plane and full on-prem or VPC deployment, which eliminates reliance on our shared control plane.
[02:30] Laura Meier: Can you clarify what falls under "customer content" vs. "metadata"? Our legal team treats certain telemetry as customer data.
[02:45] Priya Shah: We usually classify payloads and generated outputs as customer content. Metadata like request timing, error rates, machine metrics are treated as operational telemetry. But we can map these fields for you and mark any telemetry you want treated as restricted.
[03:05] Erik Sorensen: Also, what about backups and model caching? If you do prefix caching or KV cache, where is that stored?
[03:18] Priya Shah: KV cache and prefix caches used during inference are stored on ephemeral storage in the pinned region. For longer-term caches or artifacts we recommend enabling EU-only storage buckets; in Redwood Private we can enforce that.
[03:35] Tomás Alvarez: I saw mention of sub-processors in your security docs. Who are the EU sub-processors and do any of them process data in the US?
[03:50] Maya Ortiz: We maintain a sub-processor list. Many infra providers are regionally localized; some analytics and telemetry sub-processors operate globally. We can provide the CSV. If any sub-processor requires cross-border processing we flag that for review.
[04:10] Marta Novak: We'll need that list and any subprocessors that access logs or backups. Also, do you support customer-managed KMS?
[04:22] Priya Shah: Yes, we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. With customer KMS you control keys and for Redwood Private we can integrate with your KMS endpoints in your VPC.
[04:40] Laura Meier: Encryption in transit and at rest required. Also need FIPS 140-2 compatible HSM for certain keys. Do you support that?
[04:55] Jesse Kim: We do support HSM-backed keys and can work with FIPS-compliant providers. That is part of our enterprise security offering and usually included with Private deployments; we'll share the HSM/KMS integration guide.
[05:10] [05:10] Speaker 2 (transcription noise): umm hm
[05:13] Tomás Alvarez: About audit logs: are logs tamper-evident and do you provide immutable retention? We need long retention for forensics and audit.
[05:28] Priya Shah: Audit logs are exported to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets or to your SIEM via secure connectors. We can make the export append-only and sign logs to provide tamper evidence. Retention policy is configurable.
[05:47] Laura Meier: Good. Another concern: model weights — if you're hosting a model for us in EU, where are the weights stored and who can access them?
[06:00] Priya Shah: Model artifacts are stored in region-pinned storage. Access is controlled via RBAC and tenant isolation; only your tenant's service accounts and admin roles can access them. Redwood's ops staff have limited emergency access which is audited and requires approvals; this is covered in the SOC2/ISO reports and in our support runbooks.
[06:22] Marta Novak: We will want explicit statements about human access and process for emergency access, plus the ability to restrict that access for our private deployment.
[06:35] Jesse Kim: Absolutely, we can provide the break-glass policy and the audit trail for any human access. In Private deployments you can choose to completely disallow Redwood staff access, and support is done via customer-provided diagnostics.
[06:50] [06:50] Interruption - background noise
[06:55] Erik Sorensen: Another technical detail — how do you route requests when a model isn't available in EU region? Do you have model variants or fallbacks?
[07:08] Priya Shah: We support model variant routing. For strict EU-only pinning you can set a hard block (reject requests if model not available) or a soft fallback to a compatible EU-hosted model variant. Hard block ensures zero cross-border processing.
[07:26] Tomás Alvarez: Latency is a concern — EU-only routing might affect throughput, what's your SLA for pinned regions?
[07:38] Jesse Kim: For Dedicated capacity we provide region-specific SLAs. For hosted EU-only we publish performance profiles per region. We can run a benchmark during the POC to validate latency SLOs for your workloads.
[07:53] Laura Meier: Okay. On the legal side, cross-border transfer clauses — do you rely on SCCs or do you offer data processing addenda that specify no transfer?
[08:06] Marta Novak: (correcting) we need the mechanism.
[08:10] Jesse Kim: We support standard SCCs and can include explicit contractual region restrictions in the DPA. For absolute guarantees, Private deployment is recommended where data never leaves your environment.
[08:25] Tomás Alvarez: Can you confirm if any telemetry sent to Redwood control plane includes PII or customer identifiers? We prefer pseudonymized telemetry only.
[08:38] Priya Shah: By default control plane telemetry is pseudonymized; we can switch to fully anonymized. We'll provide the telemetry field map so you can decide which fields are safe.
[08:52] [09:00] Speaker 1: uh-huh
[09:02] Laura Meier: About sub-processors again — we require 30 days notice before adding new sub-processors for regulated workloads. Is that possible?
[09:11] Maya Ortiz: We can commit to notification windows in the contract; 30 days notice is feasible for most infra changes. We'll surface exceptions if any immediate security fixes require urgent changes with notification and mitigation steps.
[09:28] Marta Novak: We will also want a full list of EU-region data centers and provider locations for our auditors.
[09:36] Priya Shah: We'll send the region map and data center locations we use for EU pinned deployments.
[09:44] Tomás Alvarez: For the demo/proof of concept, can you spin up an EU-only test environment with our keys and show region-pinned logs?
[09:55] Jesse Kim: Yes, Priya can provision a demo VPC with customer KMS integration; we'll show end-to-end pinned routing and audit log exports.
[10:05] Priya Shah: I'll need Tomás' list of required regions and any IP allowlists — I'll start the infra request after the call.
[10:15] Tomás Alvarez: I'll send that today.
[10:18] [10:18] Minor crosstalk
[10:22] Laura Meier: One more question — retention policies for request-level data. We need the ability to purge on demand for specific records.
[10:33] Priya Shah: We support targeted record purge for customer content; for logs that have been exported to your buckets you'd manage retention there. For hosted where we store short-term logs in region we can also perform purge actions and provide receipts.
[10:50] Marta Novak: Do you have a data subject access request (DSAR) process documented? We need timelines for response.
[10:58] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we have a DSAR playbook; typical turnaround is 30 days, and we can compress timelines for enterprise contracts. We'll include that doc.
[11:10] [11:10] Speaker label error
[11:12] Erik Sorensen: From an infra perspective, network egress — can you restrict any third-party callbacks to EU endpoints only?
[11:22] Priya Shah: Yes, outbound callbacks can be restricted to EU destinations, and we can enforce egress allowlists per deployment.
[11:33] Laura Meier: Any concerns about subprocessor change mid-contract? We need to ensure continuity.
[11:41] Jesse Kim: We generally provide migration plans and can grandfather in critical subprocessors or offer Private deployments to avoid churn.
[11:52] [12:00] Brief pause
[12:05] Marta Novak: On certification evidence — besides SOC2 Type II, do you have ISO 27001 and penetration test reports available?
[12:15] Priya Shah: Yes, both. We'll include redacted penetration test summaries and ISO certificate in the packet. Full pentest artifacts are provided under NDA.
[12:26] Tomás Alvarez: For the POC, will you let us run our own benchmarks including load and latency from EU clients?
[12:36] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll coordinate a time window for a bench run and give you test endpoints in the EU-only environment.
[12:45] Laura Meier: Great. Any multi-tenant risk — can other tenants' models or workload cause data leakage?
[12:55] Jesse Kim: We do strong tenant isolation in the runtime; model weights and KV caches are namespaced. For customers with extremely high isolation needs we recommend Private where you get dedicated pools.
[13:10] [13:10] Background typing
[13:15] Erik Sorensen: How do you handle data deletion for models that have been fine-tuned with our prompts?
[13:24] Priya Shah: Fine-tuned artifacts are stored per-tenant and can be deleted on request. We also track provenance so we can confirm deletion. For shared baseline models we can't alter the upstream weights but your tenant-specific fine-tunes are removable.
[13:41] Laura Meier: Ok. Let's summarize next steps...
[13:46] Jesse Kim: Sure, recap: Redwood shares SOC2/ISO and pentest redacted reports; SE provisions EU-only demo with customer KMS; NordicBank reviews sub-processor list and confirms blockers; legal follow-up call to nail contract language.
[14:04] Marta Novak: That matches our expectations. We'll target the dates discussed.
[14:11] Jesse Kim: Perfect. Anything else?
[14:14] [14:14] Minor crosstalk
[14:18] Laura Meier: No, thanks everyone.
[14:20] Jesse Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc packet and schedule the POC spin-up.
